papers.title_in_file: Evaluating the Impact of Different Quantum Kernels on the Classification Performance of Support Vector Machine Algorithm: A Medical Dataset Application
papers.version_note: The text layer lost the Greek and math glyphs (rotation-gate names print as private-use characters), and Table 1 and Figure 1 are images. The gate names of the best and worst feature maps therefore cannot be read; their values in Table 1 are not in the text layer.
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study that runs a simulated QSVM-Kernel (PennyLane, scikit-learn SVM) with 9 quantum feature maps on the Wisconsin Breast Cancer (original) and TCGA Glioma datasets and compares accuracy, AUROC and total execution time.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset has 699 patients (Benign: 458, Malignant: 241), and that the TCGA dataset has 839 patients after exclusions, 487 belonging to LGGs and 352 belonging to HGGs.
quotes: The Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset has 699 patients (Benign: 458, Malignant: 241)
The remaining dataset contain information for a total of 839 patients, with 487 belonging to LGGs and the remaining 352 belonging to HGGs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own datasets in Section II.A.

assertions.value: The authors state that both datasets were compressed with PCA and that the first 5 dimensions represent the raw data, and that PCA does not guarantee the selection of the most discriminative components.
quotes: we compressed both datasets using PCA and utilized the first 5 dimensions to represent the raw data
it does not guarantee the selection of the most discriminative
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own preprocessing in Section II.A.b.
assertions.reader_inference: Reduction to 5 features limits every result below to 5 qubit-sized inputs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum kernels were computed by simulation in PennyLane 0.35.1, that the QSVMs with ZFeatureMap and ZZFeatureMap ran with a repetition of 2 on the lightning.qubit simulator, and that the other feature maps ran with a repetition of 1 on the default.qubit simulator.
quotes: Quantum simulations provided by the PennyLane 0.35.1 framework were utilized
The QSVM algorithms with ZFeatureMap and ZZFeatureMap were executed with a repetition of 2 using the lightning.qubit PennyLane simulator.
QSVMs with other feature maps were run with a repetition of 1 using the default.qubit simulator.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation setup in Section III.
assertions.reader_inference: Execution times come from simulators of two kinds, so they are not hardware times and the two simulator groups are not strictly like for like.

assertions.value: The authors state as a finding that using two-qubit quantum gates in a parametrized quantum circuit during the data mapping process significantly increases the total execution time, reducing efficiency.
quotes: Using two-qubit quantum gates in a parametrized quantum circuit during the data mapping process significantly increases the total execution time, reducing efficiency.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; no significance test is reported in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The word significantly is not backed by a statistical test in the text; times are single runs on simulators.

assertions.value: The authors state that the choice of quantum feature maps significantly influences the outcome of classification and the execution time of the QSVM algorithm.
quotes: The choice of quantum future maps significantly influences the outcome of classification and execution time of the QSVM algorithm.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical conclusion from one study on two datasets.
assertions.reader_inference: Supported by the spread between 0.98 and 0.65 accuracy on one dataset, with a single split reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study shows the potential of quantum kernels for improving the performance of SVMs.
quotes: shows the potential of quantum kernels for improving the performance of SVMs
assertions.reader_inference: The text carries no classical-SVM baseline, so the paper compares quantum feature maps with each other only.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that, because the total execution time is about 2 times higher for the parametrized circuit with equal performance, and to ensure energy efficiency in quantum circuits, it is more advantageous to use only the rotational gate on the breast dataset.
quotes: and to ensure energy efficiency in quantum circuits, it is more advantageous to use only the
since the total execution time is about 2 times higher for the parametrized quantum circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's conclusion from one study; no energy measurement is reported in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports simulator wall time, not energy.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the future they aim to develop efficient feature mapping techniques, especially for medical datasets, that affect both classification result and execution time.
quotes: In the future, we aim to develop efficient feature mapping techniques, especially for medical datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own open work in the conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the kernel matrices computed from the quantum states of feature maps significantly influence the classification outcomes of the QSVM-Kernel algorithm, so selecting an appropriate feature map is fundamentally important.
